papers.title: Physics-informed neural networks for downscaling convective-permitting rainfall extremes under sparse radiosonde initialization: a climate-analytics evaluation of tail-index distortion in dam-safety analytics
papers.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) are increasingly proposed for downscaling convective-permitting rainfall extremes, yet their behaviour under sparse radiosonde initialization remains poorly characterised for dam-safety analytics, where the upper tail of the rainfall distribution governs spillway design. We define the tail-index distortion functional, derive a bound on its bias under sparse initialization, and show that the distortion is governed by the interaction between the PINN's physics residual weighting and the effective sample size of the initial-condition ensemble. The framework is illustrated with a reanalysis-based temperature series for Lagos, Nigeria (2000–2023; 312 monthly observations; mean 26.414 °C; warming trend 0.1553 °C per decade), which serves as a benchmark for the data-provenance and uncertainty-reporting protocol that dam-safety analytics requires. Tail-index distortion should be treated as a first-class evaluation metric alongside predictive accuracy, and it identifies the conditions under which sparse radiosonde initialization produces non-conservative design quantiles. The contribution is a methodological and conceptual apparatus for auditing PINN downscaling in safety-critical climate analytics, not an empirical validation of any particular PINN architecture.

papers.title: Active-learning prioritization of rain-gauge densification under budget constraints: a computer-science evaluation of flood-forecast skill gain per instrument dollar
papers.abstract: Rain-gauge networks in data-sparse basins are typically densified by spatial coverage criteria rather than by the marginal value of each additional instrument to flood-forecast skill. the present analysis formalises gauge densification as a sequential decision problem in which a learner selects the next gauge location from a candidate set, observes a proxy label, and updates a surrogate of forecast-relevant rainfall error, subject to a fixed budget. We derive a cost-normalised active-learning criterion, the marginal skill gain per instrument dollar, and show that under a submodular surrogate the greedy policy admits a constant-factor approximation guarantee relative to the optimal budget-feasible subset. The framework is evaluated on a real reanalysis record for Kampala, Uganda: NASA POWER monthly MERRA-2 air temperature at 2 m, 312 monthly observations from 2000 to 2023, with mean 22.443 C, standard deviation 1.043 C, and a linear trend of -0.1564 C per decade. The trend is small relative to interannual variability, which we use to motivate the variance-reduction objective that the active learner optimises. We report the design of the prioritisation procedure, the approximation bound, and the conditions under which cost-normalised greedy selection diverges from coverage-maximising selection. The contribution is a computer-science formalisation of instrument placement as budgeted active learning, with an explicit skill-per-dollar objective and a provable guarantee, rather than a new empirical forecast study.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-enabled bioprinting for tumor modeling: from biomimetic microenvironment reconstruction to drug screening
papers.abstract: Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting have provided new strategies for developing in vitro tumor models with improved representation of native tumor microenvironments. This review examines the role of AI across the entire bioprinting workflow—from image-based model design and real-time printing control to post-printing functional assessment and high-throughput drug evaluation. We first outline how machine learning and deep learning algorithms optimize bioink formulation, predict the mechanical behavior of printed constructs, and enable error correction during fabrication. We then discuss AI-driven strategies for reconstructing key components of the tumor microenvironment, including extracellular matrices with tunable mechanical properties, perfusable vascular networks, and spatially organized multi-cellular architectures that incorporate cancer cells, stromal cells, and immune populations. The review further addresses the application of AI-enhanced bioprinted tumor models in automated drug screening, resistance mechanism studies, and personalized medicine, with particular attention to the integration of patient-derived cells and multi-omics data. We also evaluate current challenges, including the trade-off between biomimetic fidelity and throughput, the lack of standardized protocols and data repositories, and the need for improved model validation against clinical outcomes. Finally, we discuss emerging directions such as closed-loop optimization systems, intelligent bioinks, and the integration of bioprinting with organ-on-a-chip platforms. By providing a comprehensive overview of this rapidly evolving field, this review aims to inform researchers and clinicians about the current capabilities and future potential of AI-assisted bioprinted tumor models for oncology research and therapeutic development.

papers.title: Enhancing the bending performance of SLA-printed TPMS sandwich structures through the core topology optimization
papers.abstract: Triply Periodic Minimal Surface (TPMS) structures, e.g., Diamond (D), Gyroid (G), and I-WP, possess excellent specific strength and geometric designability, thereby achieving high load-bearing capacity and lightweight design. However, when serving as the core in sandwich structures, the uniform relative density (uni-den) design and conventionally functionally graded (con-fun-gra) design do not fully utilize the mechanical properties of materials. To overcome this limitation, a variable-density topology optimization (var-top-opt) design is adopted in the D, G, and I-WP cores to enhance the bending performance of sandwich structures, and the enhancement effects are explored. The fitting functions between the isosurface threshold and relative density are constructed for the D, G, and I-WP cells. The var-top-opt design, taking the relative density of the topology element as the design variable and the structural compliance minimization as the design objective, is performed to obtain the optimal relative density field (ORDF). The ORDF is divided into multiple segments, and the relative densities in every segment are fitted to construct the relative density function matrix of topology elements. The isosurface threshold function matrices of the optimized D, G, and I-WP cores are constructed through the relative density mapping relationship between the topology elements and TPMS cells. The D, G, and I-WP sandwich structures from the uni-den, con-fun-gra, and var-top-opt designs are fabricated using the SLA technology, followed by the three-point bending test and numerical simulation. The results show that the var-top-opt design significantly enhances the bending stiffness and energy absorption of the TPMS sandwich structures at different core volume fractions, and the improvement is larger than that of the con-fun-gra design.

papers.title: Biomechanical and fatigue analysis of a porous titanium total temporomandibular joint prosthesis with different mandibular component lengths and designs.
papers.abstract: This study evaluated the biomechanical behavior and fatigue lifetime of Voronoi lattice-structured ramus components for total temporomandibular joint replacement (TMJR) in mini (mini-TMJR), standard (TMJR), and extended (eTMJR) configurations based on the Walter Lorenz (Biomet) system, using finite element analysis. Three-dimensional models were derived from Visible Human Project computed tomography data. For each ramus length, four designs were analyzed: Voronoi architectures with 25%, 50%, and 75% filling ratios, and a fully solid design, under masticatory forces simulating unilateral left molar clenching. Von Mises stress, principal bone stress, and fatigue safety factors were evaluated. Ramus stress decreased with increasing filling ratio, ranging from 363.5 MPa (TMJR 25% Voronoi) to 71.3 MPa (eTMJR solid); all designs showed infinite fatigue life, with safety factors of 1.5-7.8. Fossa and ultra-high-molecular-weight polyethylene (UHMWPE) stresses increased with filling ratio, with UHMWPE stress exceeding the polyethylene yield strength in all models, while bone stress remained within physiological limits. Low filling ratio designs transferred more load to bone, which may reduce stress shielding, whereas the eTMJR solid design showed the lowest ramus stress and highest safety factor. Voronoi-latticed ramus components showed acceptable biomechanical performance under the simulated conditions, though long-term biological and clinical validation is required.

papers.title: Mechano-adaptive regenerative niches for orchestrating functional reinnervation of peripheral nerve defects
papers.abstract: Abstract Transcending the paradigm of passive structural support, contemporary peripheral nerve repair pivots decisively toward the deliberate spatiotemporal programming of instructive microenvironments. Integrative evidence, synthesized from bibliometric landscapes and high-resolution single-cell transcriptomic atlases, has firmly established mechanotransduction as a preeminent regulatory hub, while concurrently resolving the injury-elicited mechanosensitive phenotypic landscapes. This evidence informs a mechano-adaptive niche-engineering framework that systematically deciphers how biophysical cues govern Schwann cell plasticity, directed axonal navigation, macrophage phenotypic re-polarization, vascular integration, and global tissue homeostasis. In this context, advanced additive manufacturing platforms, notably three- and four-dimensional biofabrication, serve as foundational cornerstones for constructing biomimetic niches endowed with spatiotemporally programmable and dynamically interactive features. Collectively, these mechanistic insights are rigorously codified into rational design blueprints, wherein stiffness gradients, topographical anisotropy, and dynamic mechanical actuation converge to define next-generation neural guidance conduits. In their clinical translation, adaptive, patient-conformal, and context-responsive biofabrication ecosystems constitute transformative modalities, propelling mechano-regenerative biomaterials toward a new vanguard in neural reinnervation.

papers.title: 3D bioprinting of tissue-engineered bladder patches containing neurovascular networks using conductive microgel
papers.abstract: Current tissue-engineered bladder patches are hindered by the absence of coordinated neurovascular regeneration, which limits their functional repair capacity. This study aimed to develop a neurovascularized bladder patch (NVBP) and assess its efficacy in bladder defect repair. GelMA-MXene (GM) conductive hydrogel microspheres encapsulating adipose-derived stem cells (ADSCs) were initially prepared to induce efficient differentiation of ADSCs into neural and vascular lineages within a conductive microenvironment. These pre-differentiated neural and vascular microspheres were then formulated into a microgel bioink, facilitating the construction of the NVBP using 3D bioprinting technology. Results indicated that GM microspheres enhanced ADSCs viability, proliferation, and stemness markers (Sox2/Nanog). Upon induction, GM microspheres upregulated the expression of neural-related genes (TUBB3, MAP2, Nestin, GAP43) and vascular-related genes (KDR, ANGPT1). Transcriptomic analysis and validation results demonstrated that the PI3K-Akt signaling pathway was significantly enriched, and the expression of Tnn and Pik3cd genes within it was also upregulated. This pathway might contribute to the effect on MXene’s promotion of ADSCs’ differentiation into neural and vascular lineages. The microgel bioink exhibited shear-thinning behavior, a broad printing temperature range, and excellent self-healing and fatigue resistance. The 3D bioprinted NVBP effectively maintained stable neural and vascular phenotypes. In an in vivo rat model, NVBP significantly enhanced bladder capacity (923.76 ± 119.80 µL) and compliance (27.04 ± 5.22 µL/mmHg). Histological analysis revealed improved smooth muscle organization, reduced collagen deposition, and significantly increased areas positive for βIII-Tubulin, PECAM1, and α-SMA in the NVBP group. In summary, NVBP promotes rat bladder tissue remodeling and functional recovery through synergistic neurovascular regeneration, offering a novel biomimetic strategy for bladder tissue engineering and is worthy of further in-depth research. 3D bioprinting of tissue-engineered bladder patches containing neurovascular networks using conductive microgel

papers.title: When active learning fails, uncalibrated out of distribution uncertainty quantification might be the problem
papers.abstract: Abstract Efficiently and meaningfully estimating prediction uncertainty is important for exploration in active learning campaigns in materials discovery, where samples with high uncertainty are interpreted as containing information missing from the model. In this work, the effect of different uncertainty estimation and calibration methods are evaluated for active learning when using ensembles of ALIGNN, eXtreme Gradient Boost, Random Forest, and Neural Network model architectures. We compare uncertainty estimates from ALIGNN deep ensembles to loss landscape uncertainty estimates obtained for solubility, bandgap, and formation energy prediction tasks. We then evaluate how the quality of the uncertainty estimate impacts an active learning campaign that seeks model generalization to out-of-distribution data. Uncertainty calibration methods were found to variably generalize from in-domain data to out-of-domain data. Furthermore, calibrated uncertainties were generally unsuccessful in reducing the amount of data required by a model to improve during an active learning campaign on out-of-distribution data when compared to random sampling and uncalibrated uncertainties. The impact of poor-quality uncertainty persists for random forest and eXtreme Gradient Boosting models trained on the same data for the same tasks, indicating that this is at least partially intrinsic to the data and not due to model capacity alone. Analysis of the target, in-distribution uncertainty, out-of-distribution uncertainty, and training residual distributions suggest that future work focus on understanding empirical uncertainties in the feature input space for cases where ensemble prediction variances do not accurately capture the missing information required for the model to generalize.

papers.title: Evaluating regression models and machine learning for long-term energy demand forecasting – Germany
papers.abstract: Reliable long-term energy demand forecasting underpins energy-system planning and decarbonization policy design, yet most established methods are calibrated for short horizons and may not capture structural change. This study compares four forecasting models: multiple linear regression (MLR), a vector error correction model (VECM), support vector regression (SVR), and an artificial neural network (ANN). Germany’s final energy consumption (FEC) is projected to 2050 from annual data spanning 1992–2021. The SVR and ANN were tuned using particle swarm optimization and Bayesian optimization. Accuracy is assessed using mean absolute error (MAE), mean squared error (MSE), and the coefficient of determination (R²). The SVR achieves the highest test accuracy (MAE = 9.19, R² = 0.974), but its long-term projections substantially exceed the historical range, suggesting extrapolation instability. The ANN attains comparable test accuracy (MAE = 10.05, R² = 0.965) with stronger generalization and more plausible projections, and is therefore adopted for the base-case and scenario analyses. MLR is transparent but less accurate, whereas VECM forecasts are sensitive to the assumed cointegration rank in the small-sample setting. The ANN base-case indicates an approximately 12% decline in FEC by 2050 relative to 2008, driven primarily by fuel substitution and efficiency improvements. Across five decarbonization scenarios, projected 2050 FEC ranges from 1476 to 2195 TWh, demonstrating that transition assumptions dominate long-term forecast uncertainty. Even the most ambitious pathway, approximately 39% below 2008, falls short of Germany’s 45% FEC reduction target for 2045. The results indicate that generalization and extrapolation behavior are as important as predictive accuracy in model selection for long-term energy transition analysis.

papers.title: GA-MPC based multi-objective optimal control of overhead cranes for position tracking and sway suppression
papers.abstract: As core intelligent equipment in modern automated warehouses and high-duty industrial production, the tracking accuracy and swing angle suppression of overhead cranes directly determine logistics throughput, energy efficiency, and operational safety. In practical engineering applications, traditional methods like Linear Quadratic Regulators (LQR) often fail to balance these objectives under uncertain payload variations, while conventional Model Predictive Control (MPC) suffers from a heavy reliance on manual trial-and-error for weight tuning. The switching term in Adaptive Sliding Mode Control(ASMC)’s control law causes high-frequency jitter. To address this, this paper proposes an intelligent cooperative control strategy based on a Genetic Algorithm (GA)-optimized MPC. By incorporating real-world physical constraints (such as actuator saturation) and industrial duty-cycle requirements, a nonlinear dynamic model with load-swing coupling is established. A dual-objective MPC framework is then constructed, leveraging GA to eliminate manual tuning dependency and achieve global optimization. For computational efficiency, the controller’s internal prediction model employs small-angle linearization, while its robustness against plant-model mismatch and nonlinear sway dynamics is strictly validated using a fully coupled nonlinear physical plant. The strategy’s applicability to common industrial scenarios is validated through multi-scenario simulations under stochastic variations in rope lengths and payload masses. Results demonstrate that the strategy significantly enhances performance—reducing tracking errors by 32.74% and swing angles by 14.44%, while lowering control energy consumption, offering a reliable, and generalizable solution for fully autonomous material handling systems.

papers.title: Laser-programmed anisotropic hierarchical host bone interfaces for mechanotransduction-guided osseointegration
papers.abstract: Background Conventional mechanical osteotomy often induces thermal and mechanical damage, which compromises the biological quality of the host bone interface and impairs subsequent osseointegration. This study aimed to develop a 9.3 μm CO 2 laser-based osteotomy strategy that integrates precise bone cutting with in situ regenerative interface engineering. Methods A 9.3 μm CO 2 laser osteotomy platform was developed by combining controlled pulse-overlap scanning with gas-atomized water-mist cooling. The generated osteotomy interfaces were characterized in terms of surface topography, thermal response, microstructural preservation, and local mechanical integrity. Human mesenchymal stem cell (hMSC) alignment, focal adhesion-mediated mechanotransduction, osteogenic differentiation, and osteoclast formation were evaluated in vitro. Transcriptomic and biochemical analyses were performed to investigate the underlying molecular programs. The optimized interface was further assessed in a rat femoral defect model with porous titanium scaffold implantation. Results The laser osteotomy strategy generated deterministic microscale grooves and graded nanoscale roughness, forming anisotropic hierarchical micro-nano osteotomy interfaces. Compared with mechanical cutting, laser osteotomy reduced thermal accumulation, limited microstructural disruption, and better maintained local mechanical integrity. The engineered interfaces directed hMSC alignment and activated focal adhesion-mediated mechanotransduction, as indicated by enhanced pFAK activation, Lamin A/C reinforcement, and YAP nuclear translocation. These responses promoted osteogenic differentiation and suppressed osteoclast formation, with the Laser III group showing the most favorable biological response. Transcriptomic and biochemical analyses further revealed enrichment of adhesion-, cytoskeleton-, and PI3K-Akt-related osteogenic programs. In vivo, the optimized interface enhanced peri-implant bone regeneration, mineral apposition, and osseointegration. Conclusions This study provides proof-of-concept evidence that 9.3 μm CO 2 laser osteotomy may enable bone cutting to be coupled with in situ regenerative interface engineering. By reducing cutting-associated damage and actively programming the host bone interface, this approach shows translational potential for improving peri-implant bone healing and implant integration. The translational potential of this article 9.3 μm CO 2 laser-enabled osteotomy interface engineering integrates precise bone cutting with in situ programming of the host bone surface. This study reveals that laser-generated anisotropic hierarchical micro-nano interfaces can reduce cutting-associated damage, activate adhesion-mediated mechanotransduction, promote osteogenic differentiation, suppress osteoclast maturation, and enhance peri-implant osseointegration. These findings provide a regenerative osteotomy strategy for improving the biological quality of surgically created bone interfaces, which holds translational potential for orthopedic implant surgery, fracture reconstruction, and the repair of bone defects in clinical practice.

papers.title: Δ-HGPR: A Hierarchical Gaussian Process Framework for Active-Learning Δ-Potentials
papers.abstract: Abstract Δ-learning, which uses machine learning to represent only the difference between a high-accuracy reference and a lower-accuracy base calculator, is a promising route to high-fidelity molecular dynamics (MD) with limited training data, but it has lacked a unified protocol combining hierarchical descriptors with well-defined equilibrium sampling. We propose Δ-HGPR (hierarchical Gaussian process regression for Δ-learning), a framework for learning difference potentials, and its MD instantiation, Δ-HGPR-MD. The framework combines (i) a difference potential written as an additive radial (inverse-distance) term plus a many-body machine-learning correction, determined by a single regularized least-squares fit; (ii) the ensemble force standard deviation as an active-learning indicator with an automatically scaled threshold; and (iii) a difference potential held fixed within each round so that equilibrium NVT sampling is well-defined in both exploration and production. The many-body term of Δ-HGPR-MD uses smooth overlap of atomic positions (SOAP) descriptors with random Fourier features (Δ-HGPR-RFF). On a toy system whose difference potential contains a 1/r contribution beyond the cutoff of the local descriptor, the many-body term alone reproduces none of this force, however many features it is given, whereas the hierarchy recovers 99% of it, with a reach set by the cutoff of its radial term. In MD, the hierarchy reproduces about 80% of the shift of the ion-pair distribution toward the reference, while the many-body term alone leaves it where the base places it. On malonaldehyde and the Zundel cation H5O2+ with three base calculators, Δ-HGPR-RFF removes barrier errors of up to 0.1 eV under one protocol, giving free-energy barriers statistically indistinguishable from DFT; free-energy perturbation shows that the error contributed by the learned correction is below 0.01 eV on average in every case. For H5O2+with ANI-2x, whose dynamics collapse without correction, it recovers the Zundel geometry and a barrier and transition count consistent with DFT.

papers.title: Vendi information gain for active learning and its application to ecology
papers.abstract: Abstract While monitoring biodiversity through camera traps has become an important endeavour for ecological research, identifying species in the captured image data remains a major bottleneck due to limited labelling resources. Active learning—a machine learning paradigm that selects the most informative data to label and train a predictive model—offers a promising solution, but typically focuses on uncertainty in the individual predictions without considering uncertainty across the entire dataset. We study Vendi information gain (VIG) as an active learning policy that selects images based on their impact on dataset‐wide prediction uncertainty, capturing both informativeness and diversity. We applied VIG to two representative datasets in ecological image classification, the Kenya Camera Trap Dataset and the Missouri Camera Trap dataset, and compared VIG against common active learning methods. On both datasets, VIG achieves higher accuracy with fewer labelled examples. We further conducted extensive ablation studies to investigate the effects of the predictive model, batch sizes and other hyperparameters to find relatively robust performance from VIG. VIG has broad applicability beyond ecology, and our results highlight its value for biodiversity monitoring in data‐limited environments.

papers.title: Uncertainty Quantification in Demographic and Health Forecasting Using Probabilistic Artificial Intelligence
papers.abstract: Reliable demographic and health forecasting requires accurate predictions and appropriate quantification of uncertainty. This study compares classical statistical models, supervised machine learning, deterministic deep learning, and probabilistic deep learning for forecasting life expectancy across 54 African countries from 2000 to 2023. The dataset contains 1,296 country-year observations and 25 candidate socioeconomic and public health predictors. Models are evaluated over one-, three-, and five-year forecasting horizons using point prediction accuracy, prediction interval coverage, and uncertainty measures. Results indicate that classical ARIMA achieves strong short-term accuracy, with a mean absolute error of 0.652 at the one-year horizon, while XGBoost provides the lowest five-year prediction error of 0.844. Probabilistic deep learning models using Monte Carlo Dropout demonstrate favorable uncertainty calibration, with the MC-Dropout multilayer perceptron achieving 96.3% prediction interval coverage at the five-year horizon. Its estimated epistemic variance share increases from 33.5% to 42.8% between the one- and five-year horizons. These findings highlight the importance of evaluating both predictive accuracy and uncertainty calibration when developing demographic forecasting systems. Probabilistic approaches can complement conventional forecasting models by providing additional information for risk-aware public health planning.

papers.title: AI and Intelligent Building Analytics for Energy Efficiency in Large Healthcare Campuses
papers.abstract: Large healthcare campuses contain dissimilar clinical and non-clinical buildings, central thermal plants and increasingly connected building-control systems. Their energy demand is unusually difficult to optimise because continuity of care, infection prevention, thermal conditions and equipment reliability constrain operational flexibility. This critical narrative review evaluates whether artificial intelligence and intelligent building analytics offer credible improvements in energy efficiency at the campus scale, and under what technical and governance conditions. Peer-reviewed hospital-specific investigations, building-energy prediction and fault-detection studies, field evaluations of predictive control, and research on digital twins and clinical indoor environments were critically synthesised. Evidence available through 12 August 2026 was considered. The literature supports a clear distinction between accurate energy forecasting, detection of actionable faults, and measured energy savings attributable to closed-loop interventions. Hospital data studies demonstrate promising predictive performance, whereas direct, prolonged, independently evaluated deployments across entire healthcare campuses remain uncommon. Model predictive control has a stronger real-building implementation record than autonomous reinforcement learning, but aggregate benefits from ordinary commercial buildings cannot be assumed to apply to operating theatres, isolation rooms or critical services. In addition, normalisation by clinical activity, sensor calibration, counterfactual measurement, interoperability and cybersecurity materially influence the validity of claimed savings. This review proposes a safety-constrained, hierarchical approach in which transparent benchmarking and diagnostics precede supervised optimisation and carefully governed campus-level coordination. Future investigations should report whole-campus and zone-level outcomes, seasonal persistence, uncertainty, clinical environmental compliance, equipment reliability and carbon consequences under reproducible evaluation designs. Intelligent analytics should therefore be understood as a means of improving the quality of operational decisions rather than an independently established guarantee of hospital energy savings.

papers.title: A Computationally Efficient Alternative to Mpc for Real-Time Torque Vectoring in 4wid Evs
papers.abstract: Four-Wheel Independent Drive (4WID) electric vehicles offer unprecedented authority over individual wheel forces, enabling propulsion-based yaw stability control through torque vectoring. Model Predictive Control (MPC) has emerged as the dominant academic paradigm for multi-objective vehicle dynamic control owing to its constraint-handling capability and predictive horizon structure. However, the online solution of constrained quadratic programs incurs O(n³) computational complexity with respect to the prediction horizon length, rendering real-time deployment on standard automotive embedded controllers impractical for most production-grade applications. This paper proposes an architecture comprising a Sliding Mode Control (SMC) yaw stability controller integrated with a two-dimensional (2D) motor efficiency map (η-map) based torque allocator that resolves the corrective wheel torque distribution problem in O(1) time via direct memory lookup. The SMC formulates a sliding surface combining yaw rate error and sideslip angle error, deploying a boundary-layer saturation function to eliminate chattering while preserving robust stability margins under nonlinear tire dynamics and variable road friction. The efficiency-aware torque allocator pre-computes optimal torque-speed operating regions offline and retrieves them via a 2D lookup table at each control step, achieving multi-objective performance simultaneous stability enhancement and energy efficiency improvementwithout requiring any online optimization. Comparative MATLAB/Simulink evaluation under a standardized step-steer maneuver at 60 km/h on a dry surface (μ = 0.85) demonstrates that the proposed SMC reduces yaw rate root-mean-square error (RMSE) by 51.2% relative to the proportional (P) baseline, by 33.5% relative to PID, and by 37.6% relative to the Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR), while consuming only 139.8 kJ compared to the highest-consumption controller at 142.7 kJ. Theoretical execution time analysis confirms that the proposed architecture is compatible with 1 ms embedded controller cycle times on standard 32-bit automotive-grade microcontrollers, a target that MPC-based alternatives cannot reliably meet without dedicated co-processor hardware.

papers.title: Temporally Gated Active Thermography for Defect Detection in Laser-Based Powder Bed Fusion of Metals
papers.abstract: Abstract Laser Powder Bed Fusion of Metal is a key additive manufacturing technology, but its industrial adoption is limited by inherent process imperfections. While in-situ non-destructive testing is essential, current monitoring methods face limitations. In-line active thermography, as a promising testing approach, faces significant challenges with overpowering reflections from the high-energy process laser, which can saturate sensors and mask faint, defect-related thermal emissions. This paper introduces a novel stroboscopic active thermography methodology designed to overcome this limitation. The approach utilizes the Synchronized Path Infrared Thermography dual scanhead setup, which employs the processing laser as a modulated thermal excitation source. This system is based on precise temporal gating of the acquisition of the IR camera: it isolates the desired thermal emission signal from interfering laser reflections, and it ensures that the same, specific segment of the material cooling curve is consistently sampled for every measurement point. The stroboscopic approach was validated on specimens with artificial subsurface defects. It successfully eliminates sensor saturation, providing a high-fidelity thermal signal for analysis. The system identifies voids with actual mean diameters as small as 111 $$\upmu $$ μ m at depths of down to 40 $$\upmu $$ μ m. The study also quantifies the technical boundaries of the method, where signal attenuation from thermal diffusion limits detection at 120 $$\upmu $$ μ m depth to the largest defect measuring 977 $$\upmu $$ μ m.
